title: Cross-network refresh window causes intermittent authz rebinding across edge caches
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
A set of customer escalations (Hosted, Dedicated, and Private) reported sporadic cross-organization access shortly after API key rotation or token refresh events. Symptoms were intermittent: some requests observed an org-scoped token but resolved to a different tenant in downstream services for a short window (~5-20s).

Impact:
- Multiple enterprise customers reported read operations returning data from sibling orgs in Dedicated and Private setups (small number of incidents, high severity).
- Hosted customers saw elevated 403->200 flapping in traces correlated with refresh events.
- Root cause traces show mismatch between refresh validity window, edge cache affinity, and the auth proxy's ephemeral session mapping.

Reproduction steps (observed in staging):
1) Create an API key for org A and perform steady traffic through edge-hosted gateway.
2) Trigger a programmatic rotation (simulate server-initiated rotation).
3) While client obtains refreshed token, edge connections reuse HTTP/2 streams and cached session-anchor header (x-session-anchor).
4) Auth proxy accepts refreshed token but downstream session resolver used the cached session-anchor leading to an authz lookup for the previous tenant binding.
5) Results: token and session mapping temporarily out-of-sync until KV cache TTL expires or a new connection is established.

Technical root cause (short):
- Two competing caches: (1) edge connection-level session-anchor cached per TCP/HTTP/2 connection, (2) auth-proxy token-to-org mapping cached in the local KV with slightly longer TTL. During rotation the order-of-operations allowed a new token to be validated while the connection-level anchor still pointed at the old tenant, producing a transient misbinding.
- Race window widened by connection reuse heuristics (keep-alive, connection pooling) and by an optimization introduced in runtime-2.3 that favored delayed anchor refresh to reduce RPCs.

Mitigation applied (prod):
- Emergency rollback of connection-affinity optimization on edge nodes (edge-config v1.9 -> v1.7).
- Short-term increase of session-anchor propagation: force session-anchor refresh on token refresh events for all HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 reuses.
- Added a temporary guard in auth-proxy: if token age < 10s after rotation, prefer authoritative org lookup from identity-store instead of cached mapping.

Fix implemented (PR):
- Pull request: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4567 (auth: enforce session-anchor invalidation on token refresh + add deterministic reconciliation path)
- Companion PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/2103 (rollback connection-affinity heuristic + integration tests)

Rollout plan:
1) Canary on non-prod edge fleet for 24h (edge/canary-2026-03-12).
2) Gradual rollout to 20% of production edges with realtime monitoring for cross-org hits (use guardrail threshold: 0 cross-org responses per 10m per org).
3) If stable for 48h increase to 100% and remove emergency auth-proxy guard.
4) Post-rollout: include a scheduled reintroduce of affinity optimization behind a feature-flag after adding reconciliation logic.

Verification steps:
- Prometheus dashboards: auth.authz_misbind_count (should drop to 0), edge.session_anchor_mismatch_rate (should drop to baseline).
- Smoke: scripted rotation for 50 synthetic orgs in staging for 1 hour with 1000 RPS and verify no cross-org reads.
- Manual: audit logs, token/token-id correlation, and tracing spans showing session-anchor set -> token validated -> downstream mapping resolved.

Postmortem action items:
- ACTION-1: Add explicit session-anchor invalidation API in auth-proxy (ENG-98214).
- ACTION-2: Add automated chaos tests for rotation+connection-reuse scenarios in CI (ENG-98215).
- ACTION-3: Tighten TTL alignment between connection-anchor and token mapping caches (follow-up design review).
- ACTION-4: Customer communication: notify affected customers with incident summary and remediation steps (PM lead: Erika Soto).

Notes:
- This ticket covers the engineering remediation and rollout; PM owns outbound comms and CS follow-ups.
- Security has been looped in; scheduled security review on 2026-03-16.
